chunks: Muhammad b. Ali (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us from Muhammad b. Abi al-Qasim from Muhammad b. Ali al-Kufi from Amer b. Kathir al-Sarraj al-Nahdi from Abu al-Jarud from Thabit b. Abi Safiyya from Sayyid al-Abidin Ali b. al-Husayn from the Master of Martyrs al-Husayn b. Ali from the Master of Deputies, the Commander of the Faithful, Ali b. Abi Talib (peace be upon them) from the Master of Prophets Muhammad b. Abdullah, the Seal of the Prophets (may Allah bless him and his family), that he said:

Surely, Allah, blessed and exalted, has obligated you to obey me, has prohibited you from disobeying me, and has made it mandatory for you to follow my command. He has obligated you to obey Ali after me in the same way that He obligated you to obey me, and has prohibited you from disobeying him in the same way that He prohibited you from disobeying me. He made him my brother, my vizier, my deputy, and my inheritor. He is from me and I am from him. Loving him is faith and hating him is disbelief. Whoever loves him loves me, and whoever hates him hates me. He is the master of whoever I am master of, and I am the master of every Muslim man and woman. He and I are the two fathers of this Nation.

key_terms.إيمان: Faith — belief in God and His appointed guides
key_terms.طاعة: Obedience — the duty to follow God's appointed leaders
key_terms.معصية: Disobedience — refusal to comply with divine command
key_terms.مولى: Master/Patron — indicates authority and guardianship over the community
key_terms.وصي: Deputy/Successor — the one designated to continue the Prophet's mission

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet Muhammad say about the obligation to obey Ali ibn Abi Talib?
ai.summary: In this creedal hadith narrated through a golden chain (silsilat al-dhahab) passing through all the Imams back to the Prophet (s), the Prophet declares that obedience to Ali is equivalent to obedience to himself, as both are mandated by Allah. He designates Ali as his brother, vizier, successor, and inheritor, establishing that love for Ali constitutes faith and hatred for him constitutes disbelief. The hadith was delivered in the context of asserting Ali's divinely-appointed authority (wilaya) over the Muslim community.
